question: Once my Canadian trademark is registered, do I have to renew it to keep the registration active?
generated_answer: Trademarks are registered for 10 years and may be renewed indefinitely as long as the mark continues to be used in the Canadian marketplace. You must pay the renewal fee within the six-month window prior to the renewal deadline, or up to six months after, in which case a late fee will be applied. If you fail to pay the renewal fee and late fee (if applicable), the registration will be cancelled. For more information on renewing your trademark, please visit our Trademark e-tutorial. 1.2.10 How do I renew my trademark? You can renew your trademark by completing the Trademark Renewal Form. You can submit your form and fee by mail or in person at the Canadian Intellectual Property Office (CIPO). You can also submit your form and fee online through CIPO's Online Services. 1.2.11 What is the difference between a trademark and a trade name? A trademark is a word, phrase, symbol or design, or a combination of these, used to identify the source of goods or services. A trade name is the name under which a business or other organization operates. A trade name may be used to identify a business or other organization. A trade name may be registered as a trademark. 1.2.12 What is the difference between a trademark and a copyright? A trademark is a word, phrase, symbol or design, or a combination of these, used to identify the source of goods or services. A copyright is the exclusive right to reproduce, perform, communicate or distribute a work, or any substantial part of it, in any material form. A copyright may be used to protect a work, such as a book, a song or a painting. A copyright may be registered as a trademark. 1.2.13 What is the difference between a trademark and a patent? A trademark is a word, phrase, symbol or design, or a combination of these, used to identify the source of goods or services. A patent is a grant of a right to exclude others from making, using or selling an invention. A patent may be used to protect an invention, such as a machine, a process or a composition of matter. A patent may be registered as a trademark. 1.2.14 What is the difference between a trademark and a geographical indication? A trademark is a word, phrase, symbol or design, or a combination of these, used to identify the source of goods or services. A geographical indication is a sign that identifies a good as originating in a particular territory, region or locality where a given quality, reputation or other characteristic of the good is essentially attributable to its geographical origin. A geographical indication may be used to protect a good, such as a wine or a cheese, that is produced in a particular region. A geographical indication may be registered as a trademark. 1.2.15 What is the difference between a trademark and a certification mark? A trademark is a word, phrase, symbol or design, or a combination of these, used to identify the source of goods or services. A certification mark is a mark that certifies that a good or service meets certain standards or requirements. A certification mark may be used to protect a good or service that meets certain standards or requirements. A certification mark may be registered as a trademark. 1.2.16 What is the difference between a trademark and a collective mark? A trademark is a word, phrase, symbol or design, or a combination of these, used to identify the source of goods or services. A collective mark is a mark that identifies a group of persons, such as a trade association, that are authorized to use the mark. A collective mark may be used to protect a group of persons that are authorized to use the mark. A collective mark may be registered as a trademark. 1.2.17 What is the difference between a trademark and a service mark? A trademark is a word, phrase, symbol or design, or a combination of these, used to identify the source of goods or services. A service mark is a mark that identifies a service, such as a restaurant or a hotel. A service mark may be used to protect a service that is provided by a business or other organization. A service mark may be registered as a trademark. 1.2.18 What is the difference between a trademark and a trade dress? A trademark is a word, phrase, symbol or design, or a combination of these, used to identify the source of goods or services. Trade dress is the overall appearance of a product or service, including its shape, color, texture, and other visual characteristics. Trade dress may be used to protect the overall appearance of a product or service. Trade dress may be registered as a trademark. 1.2.19 What is the difference between a trademark and a domain name? A trademark is a word, phrase, symbol or design, or a combination of these, used to identify the source of goods or services.
